The court found that JS “had ground to fear” an attack from Hurlbut, who was then ordered to post a $200 bond to keep the peace and pay the court costs of $112.59. (Docket Entry, Ruling, 9 Apr. 1834 [State of Ohio v. D. P. Hurlbut]; Transcript of Proceedings, ca. 9 Apr. 1834 [State of Ohio v. D. P. Hurlbut]; see also “Mormon Trial,” Chardon Spectator and Geauga Gazette, 12 Apr. 1834, 3; and [Oliver Cowdery], Editorial, The Evening and the Morning Star, Apr. 1834, 150.)
